newsitem.title: USA: Peru's Fujimori to meet Albright.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori to meet Albright.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will meet on Monday with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, U.S. officials said Friday.
Fujimori is due to arrive on Saturday from Toronto, where he is to hold talks with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on the 45-day-old hostage crisis in Lima.

Guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement are holding 72 Peruvian and Japanese officials and businessmen in the Japanese ambassador's mansion, demanding freedom for hundreds of jailed rebels.
Officials in Lima had said they hoped Fujimori could meet President Bill Clinton but the White House made clear on Friday that such a meeting could not be scheduled at the last minute.

"The president of the United States doesn't have drop-by visits," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry, adding that Clinton had taken a low-key posture on the Peruvian hostage crisis on the advice of his counter-terrorism experts.
Nevertheless, hasty arrangements were made for top officials to meet with the Peruvian president on Monday morning.

Along with Albright, these will include Undersecretary of State for Political Affairs Peter Tarnoff and Clinton's longtime adviser and special envoy to Latin America, Thomas "Mack" McLarty, U.S. officials said.
The United States has voiced support for Fujimori's handling of the hostage crisis, praising him publicly for not giving into the rebels' demands.
